title: 题西林壁
englishTitle: Written on the Wall of West Forest Temple
author: Su Shi

translation: Seen head-on it's a ridge, from the side a peak
Far or near, high or low, it never looks the same
You cannot know the true face of Mount Lu
Precisely because you are standing inside it

annotations.题: to inscribe — poets wrote directly on temple walls, like public notes
annotations.真面目: true face — the real nature of something

appreciation: Su Shi turns a sightseeing trip into one of philosophy's sharpest one-liners: you can't see the mountain because you're inside the mountain. It has become the standard Chinese way of saying that being too close to a problem blinds you to it — distance is a form of knowledge.
